title: On-Demand pricing and Reserved Instances

kcs.statement: On-Demand Instances are billed per second (60-second minimum for Linux) or per hour with no long-term commitment, which suits short-term, spiky or unpredictable workloads that must not be interrupted.
Reserved Instances commit to a 1- or 3-year term for up to 72% off On-Demand; All Upfront gives the largest discount, then Partial Upfront, then No Upfront, and a 3-year term beats a 1-year term.

A Standard RI gives the larger discount but cannot change instance family; a Convertible RI can be exchanged for a different instance family, operating system or tenancy in return for a smaller discount.

A Regional RI applies its discount to matching usage in any Availability Zone of its Region and, for Linux, across sizes within the same instance family; a zonal RI also reserves capacity in one specific AZ.

problem_ideas: An m5.large costs $0.096/hour On-Demand and $0.060/hour as a 1-year RI: predict the yearly saving for one always-on instance.
